message.content:
**Moderna, Inc. (CIK 1682852) — total revenue trend, fiscal years 2022–2024**

Moderna's total revenue fell sharply and continuously over the three years, with the decline steepest in 2023 and continuing at a similar rate in 2024.

| Fiscal year (ended Dec 31) | Total revenue (USD) | YoY change |
|---|---|---|
| 2022 | $19.263 billion | — |
| 2023 | $6.848 billion | −64.4% |
| 2024 | $3.236 billion | −52.7% |

Cumulatively, 2024 revenue was about 83.2% below the 2022 level (a decline of roughly $16.0 billion). The YoY percentages and the cumulative change are my calculations from the reported figures; the dollar amounts are as disclosed.

**Source basis.** The 2022 figure is the FY2022 `Revenues` fact (id 2606883, $19,263,000,000, end_date 2022-12-31, 10-K filed 2023-02-24, accession 0001682852-23-000011). The 2023 and 2024 figures are `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` facts (id 2606789, $6,848,000,000, end_date 2023-12-31; id 2606798, $3,236,000,000, end_date 2024-12-31), both from the FY2024 10-K filed 2025-02-21, accession 0001682852-25-000022. The same 2022 and 2023 values also appear as comparative figures in that later filing (ids 2606780 and 2606789), so the series is consistent across filings and no duplicate summing was needed. The 2024 10-K's own results-of-operations table shows total revenue of $3,236 million in 2024 versus $6,848 million in 2023, a $3,612 million (53%) decrease (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:443200).

**Composition and stated drivers.** The decline was driven almost entirely by net product sales: $18,435 million in 2022, $6,671 million in 2023, and $3,109 million in 2024 (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:540800). Other revenue (grants, collaborations, licensing/royalties) also shrank, from $828 million in 2022 to $177 million in 2023 and $127 million in 2024. Management attributes the 2024 drop primarily to a significant reduction in net product sales of the COVID vaccine, reflecting lower sales volumes in Europe and the rest of the world as revenue shifted from pandemic-era advance purchase agreements with foreign governments to a seasonal commercial market; U.S. sales were relatively flat, helped by an approximately $216 million reversal of prior-year sales provisions, and early RSV vaccine sales were not material (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:444800).

**Caveat.** These are consolidated, as-reported GAAP revenue figures for calendar fiscal years; the trend reflects the post-pandemic normalization of COVID vaccine demand rather than a change in accounting basis.
